title: Serious Crimes and Counter-Terrorism (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill
what_it_is: Serious Crimes and Counter-Terrorism (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill

sections.label: Money laundering convictions annually
sections.summary: Around 70 money laundering convictions have occurred annually in the last five years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the last five years, we have seen around 70 convictions annually for money laundering.

sections.label: Entity money laundering penalty increase
sections.summary: Clauses 7 to 10 raise the maximum penalty for entity money laundering to the higher of $1 million or twice the property value.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clauses 7 to 10 amend sections 43(5), 44(5), 46(6) and 47(6) to raise the maximum penalty for money laundering committed by an entity from $1 million to the higher of $1 million or twice the value of the property involved.

sections.label: Suspicious Transaction Report penalty increase
sections.summary: Clause 5 raises penalties for failing to file a Suspicious Transaction Report to $250,000 and/or three years for individuals, and $500,000 for corporations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 5, therefore, amends section 39 to raise the maximum penalty for failing to file a Suspicious Transaction Report under section 39(2) to a fine not exceeding $250,000 and/or imprisonment not exceeding three years if the offender is an individual, and to a fine not exceeding $500,000 for corporations.

sections.label: Terrorism financing penalty increase
sections.summary: Clause 20 raises the maximum penalty for non-individuals committing terrorism financing offences to the higher of $1 million or twice the value involved.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 20 amends section 6A of the TSOFA to raise the maximum penalty for non-individuals who commit a terrorism financing offence under sections 3 to 6 of the TSOFA from $1 million to the higher of $1 million or twice the value of the property, financial service or financial transaction involved in the offence.

sections.label: Professional group penalties raised
sections.summary: For this group, the maximum fine rises from $50,000 to $250,000, with imprisonment unchanged at five years, and a higher maximum fine for terrorism financing.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For this group, the maximum fine will be raised from $50,000 to $250,000, while the maximum imprisonment term remains unchanged at five years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: These also have a high level of culpability due to their professional obligations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: They will, therefore, face a maximum fine of the higher of $1 million or twice the value of the property involved in or services rendered for terrorism financing, up from a maximum fine of $250,000 today.

sections.label: New offence maximum penalties
sections.summary: The new offence carries a maximum penalty of a $150,000 fine and/or three years' imprisonment for individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The maximum penalties for this new offence are a $150,000 fine and/or three years’ imprisonment for individuals.

sections.label: Court confiscation of undeclared cash
sections.summary: Clause 15 adds section 48FA letting the Court confiscate sums beyond the prescribed amount from a person convicted of a CBCRR offence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 15 introduces a new section 48FA to empower the Court to make a confiscation order against a defendant convicted of a CBCRR offence on any sum beyond the prescribed amount.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This means that for a person who is convicted of bringing $100,000 into or out of Singapore without declaring it, the Court has the option to confiscate up to $80,000.

sections.label: Higher composition amount for offences
sections.summary: Clause 16 amends section 60(1) to raise the maximum composition amount for offences under section 48C(2) or 48E(2) to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 16 amends section 60(1) to raise the maximum composition amount for an offence under section 48C(2) or 48E(2) to $20,000.

sections.label: Exchanging financial intelligence with Egmont units
sections.summary: This allows exchange of financial intelligence with more than 150 Egmont Group member financial intelligence units, tripling the network's size.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In effect, this will allow us to exchange financial intelligence with more than 150 financial intelligence units of overseas jurisdictions which are members of the Egmont Group of Financial Intelligence Units, thereby tripling the size of our network.

sections.label: Ban on financing terrorist training travel
sections.summary: Clause 18 amends TSOFA section 4 to prohibit financing an individual's overseas travel for training in facilitating or carrying out a terrorist act.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 18 amends section 4 of TSOFA to prohibit financing the overseas travel of an individual to any place to provide or receive any training in facilitating or carrying out any terrorist act, when one knows or has reasonable grounds to believe that the involved property or services are used to support the individual’s travel.

sections.label: Liability for abetting terrorism financing
sections.summary: Clause 21 inserts section 6B into TSOFA making those who abet, conspire or attempt terrorism financing offences liable to the same punishment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 21 inserts a new section 6B into TSOFA to make a person who abets, conspires or attempts to commit a terrorism financing offence under sections 3, 4, 5 or 6 of the Act liable to the same punishment as if the person had committed the offence under the applicable section.

sections.label: Expanded money laundering offence scope
sections.summary: The Bill expands the scope of money laundering offences and provides a more comprehensive approach to tackling the issue, which may have a cross-border element.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To make matters worse, there could be a cross-border element to the crime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill expands the scope of the offences pertaining to money laundering and provides a more comprehensive approach to tackling the issue.

sections.label: New offence for possessing property
sections.summary: Clause 11 creates an offence for possessing or using property reasonably suspected to be benefits of drug dealing or criminal conduct without satisfactory account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Additionally, clause 11 of the Bill creates a new offence for a person to possess or use any property that may be reasonably suspected of being or representing any benefits of drug dealing or benefits from criminal conduct, if the person fails to account satisfactorily how the person came by that property.

sections.label: Financing terrorist training travel
sections.summary: Clause 18 expands the offence to cover financing someone to travel abroad for terrorist training or to train others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 18 expands the scope of the offence to include financing someone to travel to another country to be trained or to train others to commit a terrorist attack.

sections.label: Higher maximum penalty for individuals
sections.summary: Clause 5 raises the maximum penalty for an individual to a $250,000 fine and/or up to three years' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For instance, clause 5 changes the maximum penalty for an individual from a fine of $20,000 to a maximum penalty of a fine of $250,000 and/or imprisonment of up to three years.

sections.label: Increased fines for non-reporting
sections.summary: Clause 5 raises the maximum fine for not reporting suspected property from $20,000 to $250,000 for individuals and $500,000 for entities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, under clause 5, the maximum fine for not reporting knowledge or suspicion of property suspected to be linked to drug dealing or criminal conduct has gone up from $20,000 to $250,000, an increase of 12.5 times.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For offenders who are not individuals, being entities, such as banks and corporations, the fine has gone up to $500,000, an increase of 25 times.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clauses 7, 8, 9, 10, 20, 22 and 23 will also impose on entities an additional monetary exposure of being fined an amount of up to two times the value of the benefits of crime.

sections.label: Sharing financial intelligence with jurisdictions
sections.summary: Clause 6 amends section 41 to let the Ministry share financial intelligence with jurisdictions endorsing the Egmont Charter and Principles for Information Exchange.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, I note that clause 6 of the Bill is amending section 41 to enable the Ministry to share financial intelligence not just with jurisdictions with which it has bilateral arrangements, but with other jurisdictions which have endorsed the Egmont Charter and Principles for Information Exchange.

sections.label: Support for enhanced enforcement framework
sections.summary: The speaker supports the enhanced framework and higher maximum penalties so law enforcement and intelligence agencies can keep Singapore safer.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: They are more information technology (IT)-savvy, and its use and execution can be very smooth and fabulous but still a form of exploitation.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I support the enhanced framework and the higher maximum penalties proposed in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This Bill is moving in the right direction to ensure law enforcement and intelligence agencies have the powers to keep Singapore safer.

sections.label: FATF national vulnerability identification
sections.summary: The FATF helps identify national level vulnerabilities.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Under this FATF, it helps us to identify our own national level vulnerabilities.

sections.label: Stakeholders upholding financial centre reputation
sections.summary: All stakeholders, regulators and enforcement agencies must uphold the reputation of a clean and trusted business and financial centre with strong anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing controls.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: All stakeholders and the industry's regulators, enforcement agencies and everyone must do our part and uphold our reputation of being a clean and trusted business and financial centre with strong anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing controls.

sections.label: CAD seized foreign illicit funds
sections.summary: CAD seized around S$164.5 million in foreign illicit funds in 2016, nearly a five-fold increase from 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The amount of foreign illicit funds seized by CAD in 2016 amounted to around S$164.5 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is a nearly five-fold increase from the previous year in 2015.

sections.label: Civil seizure and confiscation provisions
sections.summary: The speaker suggests considering civil seizure and confiscation provisions prior to or in parallel with criminal proceedings, as the activities can destroy the reputation as a trusted global financial centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As the hon Minister mentioned, these activities can have the impact of "destroying our reputation as a trusted global financial centre”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I would suggest that we consider having civil seizure and confiscation provisions prior to or in parallel with criminal proceedings.

sections.label: UK unexplained wealth order regime
sections.summary: The UK introduced an unexplained wealth order civil-based regime allowing seizure and confiscation of assets in favour of the government if a person cannot explain the disparity between known wealth sources and asset value, independent of a criminal conviction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The UK has additionally introduced an "unexplained wealth order" civil-based regime whereby, independent of a conviction in a criminal court, a person's assets may be seized and confiscated in favour of the government if he or she is unable to explain the disparity between his known sources of wealth and the value of his assets.

sections.label: Freezing order for economic crime
sections.summary: A proposal is being consulted on whereby a person charged in Court for an economic crime is also given a freezing order of assets amounting to the same amount alleged to have been gained from the economic crime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Specifically, it is consulting on a proposal whereby a person who is charged in Court for an economic crime, is also visited with a "freezing order" of his assets amounting to the same amount that he is alleged to have gained from the economic crime.

sections.label: Parallel money laundering prosecution
sections.summary: Authorities should consider parallel money laundering prosecution at charging so unexplained wealth may be frozen pending criminal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Third, at the point of charging a person for an economic crime, if he has unexplained wealth in his name, even though it cannot be specifically traced to the crime in question, the authorities should consider commencing money laundering prosecution in parallel so that the unexplained wealth may be frozen pending the outcome of the criminal proceedings.

sections.label: Ministry does not track data
sections.summary: The Ministry responded that Singapore does not track such data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The response from the Ministry was that Singapore does not track such data.

sections.label: Exchange under international arrangement
sections.summary: The proposed amendment would allow information exchange under an international arrangement, including the Egmont Group of Financial Intelligence Units.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Moving on, in respect of the proposed amendment to allow for exchange of information under an international arrangement, I note from the hon Minister’s speech that this would include the Egmont Group of Financial Intelligence Units.

sections.label: Suspicious transaction and conviction figures
sections.summary: From 2013 to 2017 STRs rose from 22,000 to 35,000, with about 70 money laundering convictions annually and six terrorism financing convictions in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: From 2013 to 2017, the number of Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) filed increased from 22,000 to 35,000.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In the same period, there were about 70 convictions annually for money laundering.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In 2016, there were six convictions for terrorism financing.

sections.label: Comprehensive regime by 2019
sections.summary: A comprehensive regime will be ready by 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: A comprehensive regime will be ready by 2019.

sections.label: Confiscating absconded perpetrator proceeds
sections.summary: Section 27 of CDSA allows a confiscation order where the person has absconded and cannot be brought back to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In response to Mr Murali Pillai's question on whether we can confiscate criminal proceeds parked in Singapore even though the perpetrator is not physically here, the answer is yes, we can.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Section 27 of CDSA allows for a confiscation order where the person has absconded and cannot be brought back to Singapore.

sections.label: Ponzi scheme money flows
sections.summary: Irregular money flows detected and shared with another country led to joint investigations uncovering over $27 million transferred to Singapore from an overseas Ponzi scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, in one recent case, we detected irregular money flows and shared information with another country.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This led to joint investigations that uncovered more than $27 million which had been transferred to Singapore from one of the largest ever overseas Ponzi schemes.

sections.label: STRO information exchange expansion
sections.summary: The proposed amendments will let STRO exchange information with more than 150 countries under the Egmont Group, up from 50 today.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will allow STRO to exchange information with more than 150 countries under the Egmont Group, compared to just 50 countries today.

sections.label: Tougher money laundering amendments
sections.summary: The proposed amendments allow tougher action on corporations and professional service providers involved in money laundering and terrorism financing, and target overseas syndicates and money mules.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As an international financial hub, Singapore is a potential transit point for illicit funds.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There are serious consequences on Singapore if such risks are not addressed.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The proposed amendments allow us to get tougher on corporations and professional service providers involved in money laundering and terrorism financing activities and target overseas organised syndicates and their money laundering operations involving money mules and other perpetrators.
